assumptions: m in {2,3,4}, b_j in {0..3}, J <= 3 (last coefficient nonzero): 189 rules

falsification: A rule with sum b < m and an infinite derivation, a rule with sum b >= m terminating from all n <= 200 with no glider, or a radix-order inversion.

history.new: Batch-firing upward sweep. After level k is processed the future depends only on the window (c_{k+1}, ..., c_{k+J}), and the window map is monotone; a window W with an entry >= m that is later dominated componentwise (periodic glider if equal) certifies infinitely many firings. Radix order = compare length, then digits from the top.
history.old: Batch-firing upward sweep. After level k is processed the future depends only on the window (c_{k+1}, ..., c_{k+J}); a repeated nonzero window is a certificate of an infinite derivation (periodic glider). Radix order = compare length, then digits from the top.

history.new: Termination from unary starts holds exactly for the 31 rules with sum b < m; every one of the 158 other rules has a periodic-glider or monotone-pumping certificate; no radix-order inversion up to n = 3000.

hypothesis: H-C02-1: the rule terminates from every unary start iff sum_j b_j < m (emergent base r > 1, r the positive root of sum_j b_j r^j = m); otherwise some start produces a periodic glider. H-C02-2: for terminating rules, n < n' implies rep(n) < rep(n') in radix order.
methodology: Batch-firing upward sweep. After level k is processed the future depends only on the window (c_{k+1}, ..., c_{k+J}), and the window map is monotone; a window W with an entry >= m that is later dominated componentwise (periodic glider if equal) certifies infinitely many firings. Radix order = compare length, then digits from the top.
question: Which carry rules turn unary numerals into finite normal forms, what is the emergent base, and are the resulting representations ordered like ordinary numerals?
